title: MCP projector reconcile
scope: Actual projector run as a child process against temporary registry/target/ledger triples with a fresh environment. No live .mcp.json was modified, no MCP server was launched and no boot ran.

defects_closed.D1_deleted_definition_leaked: An ownership ledger (sidecar JSON, MCP_PROJECTION_STATE) records the names this projector owns; an owned name that is no longer a projector-managed registry definition is removed from the target and recorded in the ledger deletion history. Entries the projector has never owned are never touched, so bespoke servers are preserved.
defects_closed.D2_no_schema_validation: validateRegistry() checks root shape, managed-by vocabulary, gate grammar, requires grammar, transport (command or url), args/env/headers types. Every error is enumerated before anything is written.
defects_closed.D3_malformed_input_exited_zero: Unreadable/unparseable/schema-invalid registry now exits 2 with the target byte-identical; target read or write failure exits 3. Boot is unaffected: the entrypoint pipes the script and appends || true, so the FAIL line surfaces without aborting.
defects_closed.D4_missing_requires_removed_entry: requiresMet() is total and always returns {ok, why, explicit}; an absent or null requirements array is the empty requirement set and is reported explicitly in the run summary.

also_changed: binOnPath() no longer shells out to `command -v $name`; PATH is walked in-process with fs.accessSync, so no registry-controlled string reaches a shell.
atomicity: Target and ledger are replaced by write-to-temp + fsync + rename(2) in the same directory, preserving the previous file mode. A failure leaves the previous file intact and removes the temp file (asserted).
